title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the second part of the notes following 'La Longue Marche', titled 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'. The page is bookkeeping inside a group-scheme formalism. G is a reductive group scheme with a 'determinant' δ_G: G → G_m; GL_2 is the evident model. SG = Ker δ_G plays the role of SL_2, μ_2 is the sign group, and G^{±1} := Ker δ_G^2 is the group of elements with determinant ±1. ρ and σ are two automorphisms, plausibly involutions, attached to a torus T_ρ and to a group N'_σ (perhaps a normaliser-type group). Each carries a character: δ_ρ on T_ρ, and δ_σ, ε_σ on N'_σ.

The previous page (451) defines an extension M_{ρ,σ} = (R_{ρ,σ} × SG)/μ_2. It also defines the quotients T_{ρ,σ} = M_{ρ,σ}/SG, together with their variants °, + and +°.

Item (151) records the identifications T_{ρ,σ} ≅ R_{ρ,σ}/μ_2 and T°_{ρ,σ} ≅ R°_{ρ,σ}/μ_2, and T⁺ ≅ SR_{ρ,σ}, T^{+°} ≅ SR°_{ρ,σ}. Paragraph 80 then coordinatises a point 𝔘 of M_{ρ,σ} through the projections Θ_G, Θ_ρ, Θ_σ and the characters δ, ε_ρ, ε_σ, giving the data (152):
- U ∈ ΓG, a ∈ ΓT_ρ, b ∈ ΓN'_σ;
- ε, ε' ∈ Γμ_2;
- μ ∈ ΓG_m.

These are subject to (152'): μ = δ_G(U) = δ_σ(b) = ε δ_ρ(a), and ε' = ε_σ(b). The point is that ε, ε' and μ are determined by (U, a, b) alone. A marginal note says one should still verify that (152') cuts out M_{ρ,σ} exactly as a subgroup of G × T_ρ × N'_σ.

The second half translates these coordinates into the notation of §46 and following. There one has u ∈ T_0 (a torus mapped isomorphically to G_m by δ_G, so G = T_0 ⋉ SG), α, α_0 ∈ G^{±1}, and β, β_0, f ∈ SG. The dictionary (154) reads: α = u a^{-1}, β = u b^{-1}, U = f^{-1} u, α_0 = f^{-1} α, β_0 = f^{-1} β. These are formulas inside G, so they need embeddings T_ρ, N'_σ ↪ G; the next page makes this explicit.

A margin entry (153) proposes the twisted-commutator / coboundary-type quantities ξ = αρ(α)^{-1}, η = εβσ(β)^{-1}, and likewise g = α_0ρ(α_0)^{-1}, h = εβ_0σ(β_0)^{-1}.

Determinant check: det α = μ/(εμ) = ε ∈ μ_2, so α ∈ G^{±1}; det β = μ/μ = 1, so β ∈ SG. Both are consistent with the claimed membership. The purpose is to relate the new 'intrinsic' description of the symmetry group M_{ρ,σ} to the earlier explicit parametrisation of solutions of the loop equation.
errors: The 'i.e.' line reads u = α a^{-1} = β b. From α = u a^{-1} one gets u = α a, not α a^{-1}. Either this is a slip, or the exponent is misread.

Points flagged by Grothendieck himself in the margin: that (152') characterises M_{ρ,σ} as a subgroup of G × T_ρ × N'_σ is asserted but not verified. The formulas (154) only make sense after choosing embeddings T_ρ, N'_σ ↪ G and the torus T_0; this is addressed on the next page.

ideas.what: Presentation of the symmetry group M_{ρ,σ} = (R_{ρ,σ} × SG)/μ_2 by coordinates (U, a, b) with determinant/sign compatibility conditions
ideas.modern_name: fibre product / subgroup of a product cut out by character equations; central extension by μ_2

ideas.what: Splitting G = T_0 ⋉ SG via a torus T_0 mapped isomorphically to G_m by the determinant, giving unique factorisation U = f^{-1}u
ideas.modern_name: semidirect product decomposition GL_n = G_m ⋉ SL_n

ideas.what: Twisted coboundary expressions αρ(α)^{-1} and εβσ(β)^{-1} attached to automorphisms ρ, σ

deep.surprise_reason: The page is notational bookkeeping: a dictionary between two parametrisations of a symmetry group in the loop-equation study, plus determinant/sign compatibilities. The broader 'équation des lacets' manuscript is little studied, but this page contains no substantive new result or connection.
transcription_corrections: The margin formulas (153) read ξ = αρ(α)^{-1}, η = εβσ(β)^{-1} (alpha, not 'a').
The long margin note reads roughly: 'Il faudrait expliciter que ces conditions (152') caractérisent M_{ρ,σ} comme sous-groupe de G × T_ρ × N'_σ — il faudrait faire la vérification…'.
'par [-...-] δ, ε_ρ, ε_σ' contains a crossed-out word before δ. Grothendieck's own line explicitly lists 'δ, ε_ρ, ε_σ', but (152) records only one determinant μ and two signs ε, ε'.
The top line '529' is Grothendieck's own page numbering; '... fin des ...' reads approximately 'en fin des …'.
The 'i.e.' formula is probably u = α a = β b; the image is ambiguous.
